z-m-02-03.title: If both get same extra stickers, who go get how many more?
z-m-02-03.topic: Checking if difference between 2 numbers remain same when you add same number
z-m-02-03.goal: Use numbers test when you fit judge using only difference, even without starting numbers, and separate adding same to both from adding one side only.
z-m-02-03.material: Jihu and Hayun dey collect stickers. Read story one step at a time and state your idea.
z-m-02-03.thinking.0: Deciding how to judge without knowing numbers
z-m-02-03.thinking.2: Checking if answer change when condition change
z-m-02-03.prereq.0: Adding and subtracting numbers up to 20
z-m-02-03.s.s1.prompt: Info come one piece at a time. Every step choose what seem right and continue.
z-m-02-03.s.s1.hint.0: Choose small sticker numbers for both children show with picture or table.
z-m-02-03.s.s1.hint.1: Using your numbers, find difference after both get 2.
z-m-02-03.s.s1.st.0.info: Jihu get 3 more stickers than Hayun. We no know their starting amounts yet.
z-m-02-03.s.s1.st.0.ask: If teacher give each of dem 2 more stickers, how many more stickers Jihu go get than Hayun?
z-m-02-03.s.s1.st.0.after: We no know numbers yet, so being careful and saying 'we cannot tell' is reasonable with this information, and so is guessing 'the difference might stay the same'. Make we test using numbers.
z-m-02-03.s.s1.st.0.r.a: You add 3 and received 2 to get 5. Remember both of dem receive 2.
z-m-02-03.s.s1.st.0.o.b: We cannot tell yet. We need know their starting amounts
z-m-02-03.s.s1.st.0.r.b: You answer carefully because starting amounts unknown. If you try numbers, you fit see whether you really need know.
z-m-02-03.s.s1.st.0.r.c: You guess since both receive same number, difference go remain same. Na guess wey worth test with numbers.
z-m-02-03.s.s1.st.0.r.d: E look like you subtract 2 from 3. Read again say both receive 2.
z-m-02-03.s.s1.st.1.info: Now we know starting numbers. Jihu get 7 stickers and Hayun get 4. Teacher give each 2, so Jihu get 9 and Hayun get 6.
z-m-02-03.s.s1.st.1.ask: Now how many extra stickers does Jihu have than Hayun? Compare with your first idea.
z-m-02-03.s.s1.st.1.after: Difference between 7 and 4 na 3, and difference between 9 and 6 na 3 too. If you talk say 'we cannot tell' at first, now you see difference remain same for this example. We only test with these numbers, so think about other cases too.
z-m-02-03.s.s1.st.1.r.a: Maybe you compare number before with number after, and mix dem. Compare numbers from same time.
z-m-02-03.s.s1.st.1.r.b: Maybe you think received 2 stickers na the difference. Compare 9 and 6 direct.
z-m-02-03.s.s1.st.1.r.c: Before receive anything, di difference between 9 and 6 na same as between 7 and 4.
z-m-02-03.s.s1.st.1.r.d: 9 and 6 na different numbers. Count again, which one plenty and by how many?
z-m-02-03.s.s1.st.2.info: This is a story about two other children. Seou get 3 more stickers than Gaon. We do not know how many each has. This time the teacher gave 4 more stickers to Gaon only.
z-m-02-03.s.s1.st.2.ask: Who get more, Seou or Gaon, and how many more?
z-m-02-03.s.s1.st.2.after: When Gaon get 4, e pass all of Seou 3-sticker lead and get 1 extra. Example, if Seou get 5 and Gaon get 2, then only Gaon getting 4 make dem 5 and 6. Even if you no know how many each get, you fit judge using di difference and how many dem receive.
z-m-02-03.s.s1.st.2.r.a: You add 4 to 3. Remember say na Gaon receive 4, no be Seou.
z-m-02-03.s.s1.st.2.r.b: Difference reduce from 3 to 1. Check whether 4 received pass or less than 3.
z-m-02-03.s.s1.st.2.o.c: We no fit tell. We no know how many each get.
z-m-02-03.s.s1.st.2.r.c: Earlier when you put numbers, you see say sometimes you fit judge with difference alone. Try small numbers for this case too.
z-m-02-03.s.s1.st.2.r.d: This idea be say Gaon catch all of Seou 3-sticker lead and still get 1 more.
z-m-02-03.s.s1.reflect: At first you fit think 'we no fit tell'. When you put in numbers, sometimes na difference alone you need. If both get same amount, difference stay same; if only one side get, e change. Tell when and how your thinking change, or say if e no change.
z-m-02-03.s.s2.prompt: For Jihu and Hayun example (7 and 4), use numbers explain why difference stay same when both get 2. Add short note about wetin happen if na only one person get.
z-m-02-03.s.s2.hint.0: Write difference of 9 and 6 next to difference of 7 and 4, then compare.
z-m-02-03.s.s2.hint.1: Calculate yourself wetin happen to Hayun number and difference if na only Hayun get 2.
z-m-02-03.s.s2.selfAssess.0: You write where you check di difference with numbers you write (7, 4, 9, 6, and so on)?
z-m-02-03.s.s2.selfAssess.1: You give reason say both children increase by same amount?
z-m-02-03.s.s2.selfAssess.2: You also say difference change when na only one side receive?
z-m-02-03.s.s2.model.0: With 7 and 4, if both receive 2, dem become 9 and 6, so difference remain 3. Both increase by same amount, so Jihu 3 more no change. If only Hayun receive, difference reduce.
z-m-02-03.s.s2.model.1: If you see Jihu as Hayun 4 plus 3 extra, even if both receive 2, Jihu still get 3 more. If only one side receive, di difference change by 3.

z-m-02-01.title: Two pencils wey we never line up together: which one long pass?
z-m-02-01.topic: Chaining length comparisons and judging whether information enough
z-m-02-01.goal: Separate when you fit chain comparison results wey you know and when you need compare more; talk what else to compare to settle am.
z-m-02-01.material: Four new pencils dey on group desk. Their tags na 가, 나, 다, 라. To compare lengths, dem straighten all pencils and line up one end. So far, dem only compare two pairs side by side. First, 가 longer than 나. Second, 나 longer than 다. Dem never put 가 and 다 side by side, and 라 never compare with any pencil.
z-m-02-01.thinking.0: Chaining comparisons wey you already know to get new conclusion
z-m-02-01.thinking.2: Choosing next comparison wey dem need to decide
z-m-02-01.prereq.0: Comparing 'longer/shorter' by putting two things end to end (Grade 1 level)
z-m-02-01.s.s1.prompt: Dem never put 가 and 다 side by side. Which pencil we fit say longer?
z-m-02-01.s.s1.hint.0: Line up 가, 나, 다 from longest to shortest and write the order.
z-m-02-01.s.s1.hint.1: For your order, compare positions of 가 and 다.
z-m-02-01.s.s1.o.a: We no know yet. We need put both side by side
z-m-02-01.s.s1.r.a: Direct test go give sure answer, true. But before saying 'we no know yet,' see if you fit chain two comparisons wey you already know.
z-m-02-01.s.s1.o.b: 다 longer. E the last pencil wey dem bring out
z-m-02-01.s.s1.r.b: Order wey pencils appear in story no concern length. Only comparisons saying which pencil longer count as evidence.
z-m-02-01.s.s1.o.c: 가 longer. We fit know by chaining comparisons
z-m-02-01.s.s1.r.c: Dis chain two comparisons: 가 longer than 나, and 나 longer than 다.
z-m-02-01.s.s1.o.d: Dem same length because we never put dem side by side
z-m-02-01.s.s1.r.d: Not putting dem side by side no be evidence say lengths same. You must use comparison results to say whether same or different.
z-m-02-01.s.s1.explain: 가 longer than 나, and 나 longer than 다. If dem line up from longest, first 가, then 나, then 다. So 가 longer than 다. You fit test directly too, but before that, you fit find am by chaining comparisons you know.
z-m-02-01.s.s2.prompt: New information: dem put 다 and 라 side by side, and 라 longer than 다. So which longer, 가 or 라?
z-m-02-01.s.s2.hint.0: Line up 가, 나, 다, 라 from longest to shortest. Draw at least 2 possible orders.
z-m-02-01.s.s2.hint.1: Move 라 position and check whether both old comparisons and new one still hold.
z-m-02-01.s.s2.o.a: 가 longer. 가 na first pencil wey come out
z-m-02-01.s.s2.r.a: Being first to come out no reason about length. Check whether any comparison connect 가 and 라.
z-m-02-01.s.s2.o.b: We no know yet. No comparison connect 가 and 라
z-m-02-01.s.s2.o.c: We no fit tell. First we must put 가 and 다 side by side again
z-m-02-01.s.s2.r.c: We don already decide say 가 longer than 다. Wetin remain undecided na between 가 and 라.
z-m-02-01.s.s2.o.d: 라 longer because na comparison we learn last
z-m-02-01.s.s2.r.d: You no fit say e longer because na later comparison we learn. Wetin we learn only be say 라 longer than 다.
z-m-02-01.s.s2.explain: We only know both 가 and 라 longer than 다. Even if both longer than 다, this comparison alone no decide which of 가 and 라 longer. We need put 가 and 라 side by side or get another comparison wey connect dem.
z-m-02-01.s.s3.prompt: Which two pencils you fit put side by side to find whether 라 longer than 가? Write one way and what result go let you know.
z-m-02-01.s.s3.hint.0: First check whether comparisons we know directly connect 가 and 라.
z-m-02-01.s.s3.hint.1: Choose put 라 beside one of 가, 나, 다, and think separately when 라 longer and when e shorter.
z-m-02-01.s.s3.selfAssess.0: If you put two pencils wey you choose side by side, go e decide which of 가 and 라 longer?
z-m-02-01.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You work out whether any result still go leave us not knowing?
z-m-02-01.s.s3.selfAssess.2: You notice, like model answer 2, another way na add condition, say 'we fit know only if result be like this'?
z-m-02-01.s.s3.model.0: Put 라 and 가 side by side. If you compare both pencils directly, you go know at once which longer.
z-m-02-01.s.s3.model.1: Put 라 next to 나. If 라 shorter than 나, 가 longer than 나, so you know 가 longer. If 라 longer than 나, we still no know.
z-m-02-01.s.s3.modelNote.1: This answer also talk say result fit settle am, or we fit still no know.

z-m-02-07.title: If groups of 2 come out exact, groups of 3 go come out exact too?
z-m-02-07.topic: Rule for number of people wey meet the conditions about wetin remain when dem group them by 2 and by 3
z-m-02-07.goal: Change the number of people by yourself and check say one grouping coming out exact no mean say the other one go too, then find plenty numbers wey meet both conditions and talk their rule.
z-m-02-07.material: For gym class, make the number of students for our group be n. n dey from 2 to 30. Soyul talk say, 'If nobody remain when we make pairs of 2, nobody go remain when we make groups of 3 too.'
z-m-02-07.thinking.0: Check directly whether e always be so
z-m-02-07.thinking.1: Find plenty answers wey meet both conditions together
z-m-02-07.thinking.2: Find the rule inside the answers wey you find
z-m-02-07.prereq.0: Count by grouping into 2s and 3s, with numbers up to 30 (Grade 2 level)
z-m-02-07.s.s1.prompt: Wetin you think about wetin Soyul talk?
z-m-02-07.s.s1.hint.0: Change the number of people to 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 and make table.
z-m-02-07.s.s1.hint.1: For the table, write how many remain when you make groups of 3 for each number of people.
z-m-02-07.s.s1.o.a: Correct. If the number of people fit pair by twos, e go always divide exact by threes too.
z-m-02-07.s.s1.r.a: Calculation for one or two numbers of people no mean say e go work for every number. Dem no try dividing by threes as dem change the number of people.
z-m-02-07.s.s1.o.b: Wrong. Any number of people wey divide exact by twos go always get something wey remain when dem divide am by threes.
z-m-02-07.s.s1.r.b: 6 people divide exact by twos and by threes. Test whether some cases get remainder and some no get.
z-m-02-07.s.s1.o.c: E no always work. You must try divide as you change the number of people.
z-m-02-07.s.s1.o.d: Correct. The bigger the group, the easier e be to divide exact by threes.
z-m-02-07.s.s1.r.d: More people no mean say e go divide exact. You fit find out by dividing each number of people directly.
z-m-02-07.s.s1.explain: 6 people come out exact as 3 pairs of 2 and 2 groups of 3. But 10 people come out exact as 5 pairs of 2, while for groups of 3 dem be 3 groups with 1 person remaining. Even if some cases fit, e no be 'always', and one case wey no fit don enough.
z-m-02-07.s.s2.prompt: Find 3 different numbers of students n wey no person remain when dem make pairs of 2, and exactly 1 person remain when dem make groups of 3. (2 or more and 30 or less)
z-m-02-07.s.s2.hint.0: Increase the number of people one by one, make pairs of 2 and groups of 3, then write the number wey remain for table.
z-m-02-07.s.s2.hint.1: For the table, choose the numbers of people wey meet the conditions for both rows.
z-m-02-07.s.s2.fail.c1: Abeg use natural number from 2 to 30.
z-m-02-07.s.s2.ok.c2: Nobody remain when dem make pairs of 2.
z-m-02-07.s.s2.fail.c2: 1 person remain when dem make pairs of 2. The number of people must fit exactly into pairs of 2.
z-m-02-07.s.s2.ok.c3: 1 person remain when dem make groups of 3.
z-m-02-07.s.s2.fail.c3: The number wey remain when dem make groups of 3 no be exactly 1.
z-m-02-07.s.s2.explain: The numbers of people wey meet the conditions na 4, 10, 16, 22, 28. For example, 10 people make 5 pairs of 2, and for groups of 3 na 3 groups with 1 person remaining. With 7 people, 1 remain in pairs of 2, and with 12 people nobody remain in groups of 3.
z-m-02-07.s.s2.because.prompt: If you put the numbers of people wey you find side by side from the smallest, wetin rule you see? Write wetin you see.
z-m-02-07.s.s2.because.hint.0: Calculate the gap between each number you find one after the other, and write the difference between neighboring numbers.
z-m-02-07.s.s2.because.hint.1: Check whether all the differences dey the same, and think where that size fit come from.
z-m-02-07.s.s2.because.selfAssess.0: You check say the numbers wey I find dey all increase by the same amount?
z-m-02-07.s.s2.because.selfAssess.1: You think whether that amount get connection with the number of people wey fit come out exact in pairs of 2 and groups of 3 (6 people)?
z-m-02-07.s.s2.because.selfAssess.2: You guess whether the same rule go continue for numbers greater than 30?
z-m-02-07.s.s2.because.model.0: Dem dey increase by 6, like 4, 10, 16, 22, 28. Group of 6 fit come out exact in pairs of 2 and groups of 3, so if you add 4 people to am, e seem to meet the conditions.
z-m-02-07.s.s2.because.model.1: Each time, e go from 4 to 10 to 16, adding 6. E dey continue with the same gap, and after 28 I think say e go be 34.

z-m-02-04.title: Square blocks: does each new level add same number of blocks?
z-m-02-04.topic: Check how the added number changes with each new step.
z-m-02-04.goal: Decide whether one observation enough to say 'it keeps increasing by same amount.' Count more cases to state rule and predict next.
z-m-02-04.material: Build square shape with blocks. Level 1 has 1 block. Level 2 has 2 across and 2 rows, 4 total. Build levels 3 and 4 same way. Doyun says, "Level 1 has 1 and level 2 has 4. Each added level adds 3 blocks!"
z-m-02-04.thinking.0: Stop before making general rule from one example.
z-m-02-04.thinking.1: Count more cases to gather evidence.
z-m-02-04.thinking.2: Use the rule you find to predict next case.
z-m-02-04.prereq.1: Count blocks and check how number grow.
z-m-02-04.s.s1.prompt: Wetin you think about Doyun claim based only on 1-step and 2-step stairs shown so far?
z-m-02-04.s.s1.hint.0: First build 1-level and 2-level using blocks or drawing.
z-m-02-04.s.s1.hint.1: Build 3-level same way and count all blocks.
z-m-02-04.s.s1.o.a: Correct. From now, e go keep adding 3 each time.
z-m-02-04.s.s1.r.a: You saw only one change, from 1 to 2 steps, and assumed e go continue. You never count whether 3 and 4 steps do same.
z-m-02-04.s.s1.o.b: Wrong. Each new level always adds 4 blocks.
z-m-02-04.s.s1.r.b: Dem choose another rule without counting. Count 3-level and 4-level to see which statement correct.
z-m-02-04.s.s1.o.c: We no know yet. We must count all way to 100 levels.
z-m-02-04.s.s1.r.c: You no need go that far. Count a few more levels to see if claim fail.
z-m-02-04.s.s1.o.d: We no know yet. We must count blocks for 3-level and 4-level too.
z-m-02-04.s.s1.explain: Doyun check only once, from 1 step to 2. One observation no enough to say it continues. Add 3 and 4 steps and count to check claim.
z-m-02-04.s.s2.prompt: 3-level has 9 blocks and 4-level has 16. Write block increases from 1 to 2 levels, 2 to 3, and 3 to 4. Wetin you get?
z-m-02-04.s.s2.hint.0: Write block counts for levels 1 to 4 in one line, and the increase between neighboring counts.
z-m-02-04.s.s2.hint.1: Put added numbers side by side and check whether dem same or different.
z-m-02-04.s.s2.r.a: If you follow wetin Doyun talk exactly, na this go happen. Check if e match 9 blocks for level 3 and 16 for level 4.
z-m-02-04.s.s2.r.b: Maybe you read each level total as di number wey dem add. Find difference between previous level and next one.
z-m-02-04.s.s2.r.d: Find again di difference between 4 blocks at level 2 and 9 at level 3.
z-m-02-04.s.s2.explain: Blocks increase by 3 from 1 to 4, by 5 from 4 to 9, and by 7 from 9 to 16. Additions go 3, 5, 7, not 'always 3' like Doyun say.
z-m-02-04.s.s3.prompt: Wetin you go tell Doyun? Use numbers to say whether claim correct and guess blocks for 5-step stair.
z-m-02-04.s.s3.hint.0: Use numbers you count and separate correct part of Doyun claim from wrong part.
z-m-02-04.s.s3.hint.1: Check how added numbers change, guess next addition, and find blocks for level 5.
z-m-02-04.s.s3.selfAssess.0: You explain why Doyun statement wrong using counts (3, 5, 7)?
z-m-02-04.s.s3.selfAssess.1: Your 5-step guess come from rule above, or na number you pick?
z-m-02-04.s.s3.selfAssess.2: You fit check your guess by building level 5?
z-m-02-04.s.s3.model.0: No. Blocks increase by 3 from level 1 to 2, by 5 from 2 to 3, and by 7 from 3 to 4, so additions keep growing. Level 5 likely get 16+9=25 blocks.
z-m-02-04.s.s3.model.1: Level 5 has 5 across and 5 rows, so 25 blocks. Increase no be same every time.
z-m-02-04.s.s3.model.2: Level 3 has 9 and level 4 has 16, so increase no be 3 each time; e increase by 5 then 7. Level 5 has 16+9=25.

z-m-02-02.title: Crossing stepping stones: na only one way?
z-m-02-02.topic: Plenty ways to cover set distance with jumps of 1 step and 2 steps
z-m-02-02.goal: Show by making examples yourself say two kinds of jumps fit cover same distance in plenty ways, and talk how number of one jump type change when other type change.
z-m-02-02.material: Stepping stones cross stream. From where you start to other side exactly 6 steps. One jump fit only move forward 1 or 2 steps. No backward jump or jump pass 6. You cross only if you land exactly on other side. Yoona talk, 'E 6 steps, so only way na jump 1 step 6 times.'
z-m-02-02.thinking.1: Finding possible ways under a condition (limit on jump count)
z-m-02-02.thinking.2: Working out exchange relation between both kinds of jumps
z-m-02-02.prereq.1: Counting forward by 1 and 2 steps (Grade 1 to 2 level)
z-m-02-02.s.s1.prompt: Wetin you think about Yoona saying 'only way to cross na jump 1 step 6 times'?
z-m-02-02.s.s1.hint.0: Write jumping 1 step 6 times as one way, then change am by adding one 2-step jump, keeping total 6 steps.
z-m-02-02.s.s1.hint.1: Write step-count for each jump in order, then count all steps to check.
z-m-02-02.s.s1.o.a: Na correct. Jumping 1 step 6 times fit exactly, so no other way dey
z-m-02-02.s.s1.r.a: Finding one way wey fit no mean say other ways no dey. You never test whether you fit mix in 2-step jumps.
z-m-02-02.s.s1.o.b: Two ways dey: jump 1 step each time, or jump 2 steps each time
z-m-02-02.s.s1.r.b: You find ways using only 1-step jumps and only 2-step jumps. You never check whether dem fit mix both kinds.
z-m-02-02.s.s1.o.c: We no know yet. We need know size of each stepping stone
z-m-02-02.s.s1.r.c: You fit work out ways with only step count, no matter how big stones be. Write jump order yourself and you go find out.
z-m-02-02.s.s1.o.d: E no be only one way. You fit add 2-step jumps
z-m-02-02.s.s1.explain: For example, 2 steps, 2 steps, 1 step, 1 step add up to 6 too. If you mix jumps of 1 and 2 steps, more ways to cross dey.
z-m-02-02.s.s2.prompt: You wan cross 6 steps using 5 jumps or less total. Make 2 different ways using a jumps of 1 step and b jumps of 2 steps.
z-m-02-02.s.s2.hint.0: First choose number of 2-step jumps b, then work out number of 1-step jumps to fill remaining distance.
z-m-02-02.s.s2.hint.1: For a and b you choose, calculate distance jumped and number of jumps separately; check say both conditions fit.
z-m-02-02.s.s2.ok.c1: Number of jumps na natural number, 0 or more.
z-m-02-02.s.s2.fail.c1: Number of jumps must be natural number 0 or more, like 0, 1, 2, ....
z-m-02-02.s.s2.fail.c2: Jump distance no be 6 steps. Count all steps from 1-step and 2-step jumps.
z-m-02-02.s.s2.ok.c3: Number of jumps na 5 or less.
z-m-02-02.s.s2.explain: If a=4, b=1, then 1 step 4 times and 2 steps 1 time give 6 steps, with 5 jumps. a=2, b=2 make 4 jumps; a=0, b=3 make 3 jumps. Jumping 1 step 6 times (a=6, b=0) make 6 jumps, so leave am out because of limit.
z-m-02-02.s.s2.because.prompt: Compare 2 ways. When 2-step jumps increase by one, how 1-step jumps change? Write reason in one sentence too.
z-m-02-02.s.s2.because.hint.0: Write a and b for two methods you make side by side.
z-m-02-02.s.s2.because.hint.1: Count how much a change when b increase by one.
z-m-02-02.s.s2.because.placeholder: Example: When 2-step jumps increase by one, ...
z-m-02-02.s.s2.because.selfAssess.0: Wetin I write based on a and b of two ways I make?
z-m-02-02.s.s2.because.selfAssess.1: You give reason say 'one 2-step jump cover same distance as two 1-step jumps'?
z-m-02-02.s.s2.because.selfAssess.2: You check say same thing happen for two other ways?
z-m-02-02.s.s2.because.model.0: When 2-step jumps go up by one, 1-step jumps go down by two. Na because one 2-step jump cover same distance as two 1-step jumps.
z-m-02-02.s.s2.because.model.1: If you jump 2 steps one more time, you fit jump 1 step two fewer times and still cover 6. One 2-step jump and two 1-step jumps be same, so dem fit replace each other.
z-m-02-02.s.s3.prompt: This time, allow only 3 jumps or less. How many ways dey to cross exactly 6 steps?
z-m-02-02.s.s3.hint.0: Count jumps again for each way you already make, and keep only ways with 3 jumps or less.
z-m-02-02.s.s3.hint.1: Think how many steps you need jump on average each time to cover 6 steps in 3 jumps.
z-m-02-02.s.s3.o.a: One way. Jump 2 steps only, 3 times
z-m-02-02.s.s3.o.b: Three ways. Same as when limit na 5 or less
z-m-02-02.s.s3.r.b: Jump limit don become stricter. Among ways you make with 5 or less, drop those with more than 3 jumps.
z-m-02-02.s.s3.o.c: Two ways. Jump 2 steps 3 times, or jump 2 steps 2 times and 1 step 2 times
z-m-02-02.s.s3.r.c: 2-step jumps twice plus 1-step jumps twice na 4 jumps altogether. Count whether e fit inside limit of 3 or less.
z-m-02-02.s.s3.o.d: No. You no fit cross 6 steps with 3 jumps
z-m-02-02.s.s3.r.d: First check if you fit reach in 3 jumps by jumping 2 steps each time.
z-m-02-02.s.s3.explain: To reach 6 steps with 3 jumps or less, only way na jump 2 steps 3 times. The (a=2, b=2) and (a=4, b=1) we find before need 4 and 5 jumps, so dem no count. When new condition come, number of ways fit change.

z-m-02-06.title: Magic box wey give 4 when I put 2
z-m-02-06.topic: Choosing test values to separate input-output box rules
z-m-02-06.goal: Learn say one result fit more than one rule, den choose test numbers by yourself wey go show the two rules difference, and explain why.
z-m-02-06.material: Wen you put number inside magic box, another number go come out according to one rule. If na the same number you put inside, na the same number go always come out. We no know the rule, but wen dem put 2, 4 come out. Hajun talk say, 'Na box wey dey add 2 to the number wey you put inside,' and Seoa talk say, 'Na box wey dey add the number wey you put inside two times.' For example, if you put 3 inside, e go add 3 and 3. The numbers wey you put inside na natural numbers wey be 0 or more, like 0, 1, 2, ....
z-m-02-06.thinking.0: Not to choose rule based on one result
z-m-02-06.thinking.1: Plan test wey go show the possible rules difference
z-m-02-06.thinking.2: Reduce the possible rules with a new result
z-m-02-06.prereq.1: Add the same number two times (for example, 3+3)
z-m-02-06.s.s1.prompt: If you put 3 inside this box, wetin number go come out?
z-m-02-06.s.s1.hint.0: Write the result of putting 3 inside with Hajun rule.
z-m-02-06.s.s1.hint.1: Write the result of putting 3 inside with Seoa rule, then compare the two results.
z-m-02-06.s.s1.o.a: Na 5 come out, because e add 2 to the number wey dem put inside
z-m-02-06.s.s1.r.a: You choose based only on Hajun rule. Seoa rule also fit the result of 4 wen dem put 2 inside, but if dem put 3, na 6 go come out.
z-m-02-06.s.s1.o.b: Na 6 come out, because e add the number wey dem put inside two times
z-m-02-06.s.s1.r.b: You choose based only on Seoa rule. Hajun rule also fit the result of 4 wen dem put 2 inside, but if dem put 3, na 5 go come out.
z-m-02-06.s.s1.o.c: Na 4 come out, because the box dey always give the same number
z-m-02-06.s.s1.r.c: That one mean say if you put the same number inside, na the same number go come out. 3 no be the same number as 2.
z-m-02-06.s.s1.o.d: Na 5 or 6 fit come out. We no fit choose one yet
z-m-02-06.s.s1.o.e: We no fit know. We no know anything until we open the box
z-m-02-06.s.s1.r.e: You fit find out by putting other numbers inside. Even now, Hajun and Seoa rules still dey among the possible ones.
z-m-02-06.s.s1.explain: The result of 4 wen dem put 2 inside fit both 'add 2' and 'add two times'. If you put 3 inside, the first rule go give 5 and the second one go give 6. Other rules fit dey too, so for now we no fit choose one.
z-m-02-06.s.s2.prompt: Choose 3 different numbers to put inside the box so you fit tell whether Hajun or Seoa rule na the right one. The number x wey you put inside na natural number from 0 to 20, and e must be a number wey the two rules go give different results for.
z-m-02-06.s.s2.hint.0: Put each number wey you choose inside Hajun rule and Seoa rule, then write the numbers wey come out.
z-m-02-06.s.s2.hint.1: Leave out numbers wey the two results come out the same, then choose other numbers.
z-m-02-06.s.s2.fail.c1: Abeg use natural number from 0 to 20.
z-m-02-06.s.s2.ok.c2: If you put this number inside, the two rules go give different results.
z-m-02-06.s.s2.fail.c2: If you put this number inside, the two rules go give the same number, so you no fit tell which rule e be.
z-m-02-06.s.s2.explain: If you put 2 inside, both rules go give 4, so you no fit tell them apart from there. If you put 1, the first rule go give 3 and the second go give 2, so dem different. Every number apart from 2 fit work as test to tell them apart.
z-m-02-06.s.s2.because.prompt: Why the 2 wey you try first no show the two rules difference? And write the numbers wey the two rules go give if you put one number wey you choose inside.
z-m-02-06.s.s2.because.hint.0: Write the results of putting 2 inside Hajun rule and Seoa rule.
z-m-02-06.s.s2.because.hint.1: Put the number wey you choose inside the two rules the same way, then compare the results.
z-m-02-06.s.s2.because.placeholder: Example: 2 na ... the number wey I choose ...
z-m-02-06.s.s2.because.selfAssess.0: You talk say if you put 2 inside, the two rules go give the same number?
z-m-02-06.s.s2.because.selfAssess.1: You use numbers show say for the number wey I choose, Hajun rule result and Seoa rule result different?
z-m-02-06.s.s2.because.selfAssess.2: You think whether e go do to name just one number, and whether naming some more go make you more sure?
z-m-02-06.s.s2.because.model.0: For 2, adding 2 give 4 and adding two times give 4, so dem the same. If you put 1 inside, Hajun rule go give 3 and Seoa rule go give 2, so dem different.
z-m-02-06.s.s2.because.model.1: Wen I put 2 inside, both rules give the same number, 4, so I no fit tell them apart. If I put 5 inside, e go split to 7 or 10.
z-m-02-06.s.s3.prompt: You try put 4 inside the box. 6 come out. With this result, wetin happen to Hajun and Seoa rules?
z-m-02-06.s.s3.hint.0: Write the result of putting 4 inside Seoa rule too, then compare am with 6.
z-m-02-06.s.s3.hint.1: Also write the result of putting 4 inside Hajun rule, then compare am with 6.
z-m-02-06.s.s3.o.a: Seoa rule na correct one, because you add 4 two times
z-m-02-06.s.s3.r.a: With Seoa rule, if you put 4 inside, 8 suppose come out, because na 4 plus 4.
z-m-02-06.s.s3.o.b: Hajun rule surely correct. No other rule dey
z-m-02-06.s.s3.r.b: A result wey fit Hajun rule come out, but you no fit talk say no other rule fit give the same result. The more times you test, the more your confidence go grow.
z-m-02-06.s.s3.o.c: No be Seoa rule. Hajun rule still remain
z-m-02-06.s.s3.o.d: No be any of the two rules. None of them go give 6
z-m-02-06.s.s3.r.d: With Hajun rule, if you put 4 inside, na 4 plus 2, wey be 6. Calculate am again and check whether e match the result.
z-m-02-06.s.s3.explain: With Seoa rule, if you put 4 inside, na 8, and e no match 6. With Hajun rule, e become 6 and match. But another rule fit give the same result, so if you wan talk 'surely', you need test more numbers.

z-m-02-05.title: Locker number rule: where Seoyun explanation wrong?
z-m-02-05.topic: See how top and bottom numbers pair inside 2-row number chart.
z-m-02-05.goal: Check whether statement true for first square only also true for every square. Find wrong line and later line based on it, then rewrite them correctly.
z-m-02-05.material: Classroom lockers get numbers. Top row from left: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9. Bottom row: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. Numbers line up vertically: below top locker 1 is locker 2, below 3 is 4, and so on. Further right, top row continues 11, 13, and bottom row continues same way. Seoyun explained number rule like this.
z-m-02-05.thinking.0: Find the wrong line in explanation
z-m-02-05.thinking.1: Tell examples that fit apart from examples that disprove claim (counterexamples)
z-m-02-05.prereq.0: Counting on by 1s and 2s with numbers up to 20
z-m-02-05.prereq.1: Finding out how much greater one number is than another
z-m-02-05.s.s1.prompt: Pick one wrong line in Seoyun's explanation.
z-m-02-05.s.s1.hint.0: Write the two numbers that face each other vertically, one pair for each square.
z-m-02-05.s.s1.hint.1: Test Seoyun's statement against each pair you wrote, one by one.
z-m-02-05.s.s1.line.0: For top row, every square to the right, number increase by 2.
z-m-02-05.s.s1.line.1: Bottom row too, each time you go one square to the right, number increase by 2.
z-m-02-05.s.s1.line.2: Locker 2 dey below locker 1, locker 4 dey below locker 3.
z-m-02-05.s.s1.line.3: So bottom number always twice top number.
z-m-02-05.s.s1.explain: Wrong line na line 4. Locker 2 below locker 1 is double, but locker 4 below locker 3 no be 6, wey twice 3. E check only first square and assume all squares same. Line 5 wrong too, because e follow wrong line 4. Lines 1–3 correct because dem check each square.
z-m-02-05.s.s2.prompt: Choose all square pairs wey show Seoyun line 4 wrong.
z-m-02-05.s.s2.hint.0: For each pair, write twice top number as Seoyun said compare with bottom number.
z-m-02-05.s.s2.hint.1: Mark pairs wey no equal bottom number.
z-m-02-05.s.s2.r.a: Twice 3 na 6, but bottom number na 4. You find square wey claim fail.
z-m-02-05.s.s2.r.b: This square match Seoyun statement. Even if some examples fit, other squares can break the word 'always'.
z-m-02-05.s.s2.r.c: Double 5 is 10, but the bottom number is 6. You find square wey claim fail.
z-m-02-05.s.s2.r.d: Double 9 is 18, but the bottom number is 10. You find square wey claim fail.
z-m-02-05.s.s2.explain: For pairs 3 and 4, 5 and 6, and 9 and 10, bottom no be twice top, so Seoyun statement wrong. Only pair 1 and 2 fit. Having one example that fits does not make 'always' true, one counterexample enough.
z-m-02-05.s.s2.acc.0: Lockers 3 and 4 alone enough to disprove Seoyun's statement. Check if more squares break am.
z-m-02-05.s.s2.acc.1: Lockers 5 and 6 alone good counterexample. Check other pairs too.
z-m-02-05.s.s2.acc.2: Lockers 9 and 10 alone good counterexample. Check other pairs too.
z-m-02-05.s.s2.acc.3: All pairs you choose counterexamples. Check lockers 9 and 10 same too.
z-m-02-05.s.s2.acc.4: All pairs you choose counterexamples. Check lockers 5 and 6 same too.
z-m-02-05.s.s2.acc.5: All pairs you choose counterexamples. Check lockers 3 and 4 same too.
z-m-02-05.s.s3.prompt: Correct Seoyun line 4, then use corrected rule find number below top locker 11.
z-m-02-05.s.s3.hint.0: Choose one vertical pair write how much bottom bigger than top.
z-m-02-05.s.s3.hint.1: Check other pairs have same difference, then use it for 11.
z-m-02-05.s.s3.selfAssess.0: You check corrected statement for pairs 1 and 2, 3 and 4, and 5 and 6?
z-m-02-05.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You find number below 11 using corrected statement?
z-m-02-05.s.s3.selfAssess.2: You test corrected statement on other top numbers (for example, 7 and 13)?
z-m-02-05.s.s3.model.0: Bottom number one more than top. So number below 11 na 12. 1
z-m-02-05.s.s3.model.1: Bottom number na number above am plus 1. So e na 12, after 11.

z-m-02-08.title: Wetin we fit talk even if we no know how many people dey there at first?
z-m-02-08.topic: The result wey adding and removing people cause, no matter the starting number
z-m-02-08.goal: Even if we no know the starting number, use only the number of people wey enter and comot to separate wetin you fit talk from wetin you no fit talk, then find wetin no change by testing different starting numbers.
z-m-02-08.material: One bus stop for bus stop, and 3 people come down while 5 people enter. We no know how many people dey inside the bus at first. For other stops, nobody enter or come down. We no count the person wey dey drive the bus.
z-m-02-08.thinking.0: Separate the information wey you need from the one wey you no need
z-m-02-08.thinking.2: Check one relationship wey no change with different examples
z-m-02-08.s.s1.prompt: Choose everything wey you fit talk even if you no know how many people dey there at first.
z-m-02-08.s.s1.hint.0: Choose any starting number wey you like, then find the number of people after some come down and some enter.
z-m-02-08.s.s1.hint.1: Put the starting number wey you choose and the number of people now side by side, then compare them.
z-m-02-08.s.s1.o.a: People wey dey inside the bus now pass the first number by 2
z-m-02-08.s.s1.o.b: 5 people dey inside the bus now
z-m-02-08.s.s1.r.b: 5 na the number of people wey enter. Some people don dey inside the bus already, so you no fit talk say na the same as the number of people now.
z-m-02-08.s.s1.o.c: People wey dey inside the bus now less than the number at first
z-m-02-08.s.s1.r.c: Compare the people wey come down and the ones wey enter. The 5 wey enter pass the 3 wey come down.
z-m-02-08.s.s1.o.d: People wey dey inside the bus now more than the number at first
z-m-02-08.s.s1.r.d: Even if you no know the starting number, you know say more people enter than come down.
z-m-02-08.s.s1.explain: The 5 wey enter pass the 3 wey come down by 2. So no matter wetin the starting number be, now dey 2 more than at first, and you fit talk say e increase. To know how many people dey there now, you need know the starting number.
z-m-02-08.s.s1.acc.0: To talk say e dey 2 more than at first also mean say e increase from the beginning. You fit choose the statement say e increase too.
z-m-02-08.s.s1.acc.1: Correct say e increase from the beginning. You fit also talk how much e increase (2 people) without knowing the starting number.
z-m-02-08.s.s2.prompt: From the story say 'three people come down', wetin we fit know about the number of people wey dey inside the bus at first?
z-m-02-08.s.s2.hint.0: Draw whether 3 people fit come down if na 2 people dey there at first.
z-m-02-08.s.s2.hint.1: Change the starting number of people to 3, 2, 1 and check whether the story fit happen.
z-m-02-08.s.s2.o.a: Na exactly 3 people dey there at first
z-m-02-08.s.s2.r.a: 3 people coming down no mean say everybody come down. More people fit dey there.
z-m-02-08.s.s2.o.b: Na 8 people dey there at first
z-m-02-08.s.s2.r.b: 8 na the number wey you get wen you add the people wey come down to the ones wey enter. E no get anything to do with the number of people wey dey there at first.
z-m-02-08.s.s2.o.c: We no fit know anything about the starting number of people
z-m-02-08.s.s2.r.c: People fit come down only if dem dey there. If 3 people come down, at least how many people suppose dey inside the bus?
z-m-02-08.s.s2.o.d: Na 3 people or more dey there at first
z-m-02-08.s.s2.explain: For 3 people to come down, at least 3 people suppose dey inside the bus. So the starting number na 3 or more. Na condition wey hide inside the story.
z-m-02-08.s.s3.prompt: Make the starting number of people be a, and the number of people after 3 come down and 5 enter be b. Make 3 pairs (a, b) wey fit the story, with different starting numbers. The starting number na 30 or less.
z-m-02-08.s.s3.hint.0: Choose starting number of people, then apply the number wey come down and the number wey enter in order.
z-m-02-08.s.s3.hint.1: Write the starting number wey you choose and the number now side by side, then check which numbers of people fit the story.
z-m-02-08.s.s3.ok.c1: The starting number of people na 3 or more and 30 or less.
z-m-02-08.s.s3.fail.c1: Use starting number of people from 3 to 30. 3 people must fit come down.
z-m-02-08.s.s3.ok.c2: The number of people now fit the story.
z-m-02-08.s.s3.fail.c2: The number of people after 3 come down and 5 enter no fit. Apply the people wey come down and the ones wey enter in order, then count again.
z-m-02-08.s.s3.explain: If na 3 people dey there at first, now na 5; if na 10, now na 12; if na 20, now na 22. Even if the starting number different, now dey always 2 more than at first. If na 2 people dey there at first, 3 no fit come down, so the story no go work.
z-m-02-08.s.s3.because.prompt: Look at the (a, b) pairs wey you make side by side. Even if the starting number different, wetin no change?
z-m-02-08.s.s3.because.hint.0: For each (a, b), write how different the two numbers be.
z-m-02-08.s.s3.because.hint.1: Check whether the differences wey you write na the same all three times.
z-m-02-08.s.s3.because.placeholder: Example: Even if the starting number different, ...
z-m-02-08.s.s3.because.selfAssess.0: For all three of my (a, b) pairs, the difference na the same size?
z-m-02-08.s.s3.because.selfAssess.1: You talk say the difference come from the 3 people wey come down and the 5 wey enter?
z-m-02-08.s.s3.because.selfAssess.2: You fit explain too why starting number of 2 no go work?
z-m-02-08.s.s3.because.model.0: Whether na 3, 10, or 20 people dey there at first, now dey always 2 more than at first.
z-m-02-08.s.s3.because.model.1: The 5 people wey enter pass the 3 wey come down by 2, so no matter the starting number, dey always 2 more now.
